decisions.decision: Follow the supplied wide hero proportions: content at 15.3% from the left, a smaller logo, subtle responsive grid, and the original portrait with visible hands. Use an SVG curved crop and narrow rim instead of a white overlay, with fine orbit paths and a floating credential pill. Scale hero height with width; stack content and portrait on mobile.

Present the existing teaching process as an ICT Learning System control panel: a two-column connected module matrix on desktop and a single connected pipeline on mobile. Preserve all process titles, Sinhala descriptions, icons, and typography; use the established red signals, blue circuit nodes, technical grid, light surfaces, and dark-mode equivalents. Reveal each module independently when its row enters the viewport.

Use a primary Papers/XP switch in the compact ranking card. Preserve Full/Timing/All filters for paper ranks and provide This Week/All Time filters for XP ranks, with each mode updating its summary, rows, empty state, and destination link.

Place an admin-only batch ranking panel at the top of the student Academic tab. Limit the batch selector to the student's enrolled batches, provide Paper and XP modes with their relevant filters, show the complete roster, and highlight the open student's position and metrics.

Treat the hero and admin-managed online timetable as one continuous landing canvas rather than stacked sections: both share the same #fbfdff surface and dark-mode background with no divider or transition band, and the timetable begins with reduced top spacing. Present each class as a compact schedule card in a responsive one/two/three-column grid with restrained red accents and purposeful press/color motion. Keep the database model extensible for physical classes later without exposing that option now.
decisions.source: User-selected card direction and competitor reference, 2026-10-12

decisions.decision: Keep the original nine testimonial messages and append the eight supplied student messages as one hard-coded anonymous set named Student 01 through Student 17. Use a cohesive generated Sri Lankan student illustration atlas for the avatars. Balance every testimonial across one, two, or three independently scrolling columns so all reviews remain available at every responsive breakpoint, with a static grid for reduced-motion users.

Treat payment administration as a verification workspace rather than a flat card list. Lead with pending workload metrics, counted status tabs, and one consolidated filter toolbar; use an oldest-first queue beside a persistent evidence-and-context panel on desktop and a full-screen review view on mobile. Pending rows select the active review workspace, while approved and rejected archive rows explicitly open a full-screen details view so their original slip and audit outcome remain inspectable. Keep slip controls, student history, audit metadata, explicit approval confirmation, structured rejection reasons, server errors, concurrency protection, and real-time updates inside the review flow. Do not offer bulk approval.

Keep the Papers route as the downloadable past, provincial, and model paper library. Route the dashboard ranking card's My Papers action to a dedicated Progress screen backed by paper_marks, with type filters, average/best/latest/completed summaries, a chronological performance chart, concise trend insight, paper mix, and newest-first result history. Expose My Papers in the desktop Progress navigation and the mobile account drawer while retaining a clear shortcut to the paper library.
decisions.source: User-requested separation of paper library and personal marks progression, 2026-10-13

decisions.decision: Give paper rankings a dedicated full leaderboard route. Show overall, full-paper, and timing-paper cohorts; summarize the student's place and board size; highlight the top three; and list every ranked student with student code, average, best, and marked-paper count so duplicate names are distinguishable. Link it from the compact dashboard ranking and Progress navigation, with a route to the student's individual My Papers performance page.
decisions.source: User request for a full paper ranking page, 2026-10-13

decisions.decision: Show XP standings one enrolled batch at a time. Default to the student's matching program and exam year, allow switching among their other enrolled batches, and never combine separate cohorts on the dedicated XP leaderboard. Include every batch member, including students with zero XP.
decisions.source: User request for batch-by-batch XP rankings, 2026-10-13

decisions.decision: Present admin-managed books as one responsive PD Library system panel rather than a loose fixed-column grid. Reuse the existing CSS-3D book mockups, technical grid, restrained red/blue signals, system toolbar, and light/dark surfaces established elsewhere on the landing page. Center any number of titles with auto-fit, use compact horizontal product rows on mobile, normalize legacy Coming Soon price text into a non-orderable availability state, and avoid hover scaling or transition-all motion.

Treat device tracking as a calm security observation workspace during audit mode. Clearly state that access is not restricted, lead with student and installation counts, prioritize students who would exceed the planned two-device limit, and expose approximate browser, operating system, session count, and first/last-seen details in each student profile. Use the existing warm admin canvas, white bordered surfaces, restrained status color, and responsive table/card patterns.

Keep device enforcement opt-in per student while global audit mode remains active. Present pilot enrolment, temporary locks, student explanations, contact shortcuts, device removal, and access restoration in the student's existing Devices tab. The central Device Security workspace prioritizes open requests and locked accounts. Use explicit audit/pilot badges and calm explanatory copy so admins can distinguish observation from enforcement at every step.

Expand enforcement through capped, deterministic batch snapshots rather than automatic whole-batch enrollment. Preview eligible, already-pilot, and over-limit counts; exclude students already above the device limit; enforce the cap on the server; retain rollout history; allow cohort-only rollback; and provide a global emergency pause that preserves audit observations and underlying lock evidence. Global device audit remains active throughout.

Pair the staged rollout with a live admin health workspace and a read-focused student My Devices screen. Admins monitor healthy, locked, request, and seven-day recovery counts, drill into each cohort, and receive a warning at a 5% lock rate. Students may identify their current browser and request replacement of a non-current installation, but device removal and approval remain admin-only and server-enforced.
decisions.source: User-approved monitoring dashboard and My Devices phase, 2026-10-16

decisions.decision: Count only active browser installations toward the device limit while preserving stale, retired, and revoked records as security history. Default inactivity expiry to 90 days and let admins configure 30–365 days, run a global sweep, restore slots, retire devices, or permanently revoke them. Keep replacement approval atomic, revoke registered sessions server-side, and reuse the existing notification bell and admin realtime alerts for lifecycle outcomes.
